# Loment 0.1.5.1

**A language is not the syntax it accepts. It is the set of claims it can make about a program —
and the machinery that makes those claims falsifiable.**

0.1.5.1 closes its milestone: all 92 issues are done. What matters more is what a Loment program can
now *prove*. Memory safety stops being a mode and becomes a seven-level ladder with a named floor. A
capability stops being one interval and becomes a small algebra — shape, polarity, time. The
toolchain stops being something you install and becomes something that can replace itself from a
signed Pre-Release. A JVM stops being a prerequisite for running a Java library. And the VM stops
being judged by a stopwatch.

None of this is a promise in a roadmap. Each is an artefact in the tree, held by a criterion that was
red before the change and green after — with the reference compiler and the self-hosted compiler
producing byte-identical output for the same input.

## Install

| Asset | |
|---|---|
| `loment-0.1.5.1-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64. Unpack anywhere; `bin/loment` is the launcher. |
| `loment-0.1.5.1-windows-x64.zip` | Windows x86-64. Unzip and run `install.cmd`. |
| `loment-0.1.5.1-windows-x64-setup.exe` | Windows x86-64, self-extracting. Double-click. |
| `loment-skill.zip` | The agent guide (`SKILL.md`) on its own. |
| `SHA256SUMS` · `SHA256SUMS.asc` · `FINGERPRINT` | Checksums, a detached signature, and the key fingerprint. |

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL** — native binaries plus the standard
library.

## The shift: from features to guarantees

Most language work is additive: one more construct, one more library, one more optimisation. This
cycle went the other way. The question changed from *what can the language express* to *what can the
compiler prove about what it expressed* — and then, relentlessly, *what happens when the proof
fails*.

Three axes carry that shift:

- **Safety became a ladder, not a switch.** Seven levels, each a fallback for the one above it: the
  checker refuses what it can see, the manager prints the whole memory graph, the guarantor bounds
  constant-sized accesses, the rejector skips an out-of-bounds access and keeps running, the crasher
  ends the process without adding a symbol, the restarter brings the minimal subset back, and the
  trust floor is a seed with a name, a size and a hash.
- **Authority became an algebra.** A capability used to be a closed interval. It is now a shape, a
  polarity and a time law — ten kinds with one decision point, so that "what may this program touch,
  and when" is a question with a mechanical answer.
- **The toolchain became an artefact of itself.** A running compiler admits a signed fix-only
  Pre-Release, rebuilds at a safepoint, and remaps the live frame chain. The first executable in the
  chain is committed, and a rebuild can falsify it.

Underneath all three: the gate now compares **deterministic quantities** instead of wall-clock
stories, and the two implementations are still required to agree byte for byte. That is the part
that makes the rest believable.

## new · capability domains: ten kinds, one decision point

A capability used to be one closed interval (`capability c : disk[0..4]`). It now has three
orthogonal dimensions (`docs/306`–`docs/308`):

- **shape** — `[()..hi]` (front-infinite), `[lo..()]` (back-infinite), `[()..()]` (universal), plus
  the point domain `[a..a]` and the ordinary closed interval;
- **polarity** — `danger`, the deny-list dual of the ordinary allow domain;
- **time law** — `epoch(N)`, `far(N)`, `sliding(N)`, `decaying(N)`, `growing(N)`, `consumed(N)`.

A new statement, `tick;`, advances a virtual clock. Every law except `consumed` is a pure function
of that clock; `consumed` keeps a per-slot counter, so its width is capped at 64. All ten share one
decision point, `@__loment_guard2(cap, idx, lo, hi, kind, param, flags)`; the audit still increments
only on the pass branch, and the criterion for that now checks the shared runtime rather than one
call site.

The twin criterion builds stage1 from the committed seed and compares **both** the IR and the Potato
object against the reference for a ten-kind program — they are byte-identical. No `lom/` change: the
slice is enforced entirely on the language side.

## new · LMS: seven levels of memory safety

`docs/247`, `docs/253`, `docs/270`. Each level is a fallback for the one above, and each has
something that runs:

1. **checker** — E028 (a literal index outside a fixed array is a compile error) and E029
   (use-after-free under `lms_check`), in both compilers;
2. **manager** — `lms_report()` / `--lms-report` prints the unit's memory graph, checked against
   `gc_ladder.total_sites`;
3. **guarantor** — allocation retries once after collecting, and inline bound checks are emitted on
   `load8` / `store8` of a constant-sized `alloc`;
4. **rejector** — an out-of-bounds access skips that instruction and the program keeps running;
5. **crasher** — when it cannot reject, `llvm.trap` ends the process, and the library adds no new
   symbol;
6. **restarter** — a C program restarts the minimal subset, and stops at a cap;
7. **trust floor** — the bootstrap seed is named, sized and hashed (`docs/270`).

The default is `lms_full`; `lms` is a four-tier name, not an on/off switch.

## new · hot update: the toolchain replaces itself

`#1146`–`#1157`, ten parts. A running toolchain admits a **Pre-Release** only through an admission
predicate that is five equalities (a bug-fix-only projection, not a changelog); the release carries a
signed hotfix manifest; a two-slot loader flips atomically; the live frame chain is forcibly
remapped at a safepoint; and the projection manifest says what was applied and what was evicted. The
end-to-end criterion lands one fix in a running LSP and refuses one contract change.

## new · Java libraries without a JVM

`docs/278`, `docs/279`. `lompi` gains a foreign package kind with kind-aware identity, fetches an
index and streams artefacts over 256 KiB; `.class` and `.jar` are parsed without a JDK; a mandatory
bytecode verifier runs before lowering; AOT lowering produces Loment IR with closed-world dispatch;
a minimal Java runtime (`jrt`) supplies what the library needs with no libc and no JVM; and `lomelf`
links multiple IR inputs so the result is a Java-backed PE **proven without Java installed**.

## new · LSPE: engines, evidence, obligations

`docs/262`. The engine has E1–E4 (constants; types and capabilities; local dataflow for initialized /
alive / exclusive; interprocedural summaries), eight evidence kinds with a subset lattice, and
fourteen obligation kinds with accept sets. The solver is a worklist fixpoint with deterministic
ordering, context levels are `--lspe-level L0..L4`, and `lspe pass` is a lexical, counted audit
bypass that carries a reason. Coverage is ratcheted per kind, and an increased `pass_ratio` on the
corpus fails the gate.

## new · the `choose` matrix and a VM that counts its work

- Every legal cell of the `mode × gc × runtime × port × vm × lms × lspe` matrix is compiled by both
  implementations and compared byte for byte; conflicts are derived from what each value needs, and
  the interlock table says which construct is touched by which system, in what order.
- `runtime` / `no_runtime` is a property of the artefact, not a claim: `no_std` images carry no
  hosted symbols, and the IR itself names the row so the linker can check it.
- **The VM's gate no longer uses a stopwatch.** `lvm.Counters` records instructions, decodes, tuple
  lookups and dispatch, and the criteria compare those deterministic quantities. The fusion
  criterion, for example, asserts that `dispatches` falls (8,000,012 → 5,000,009 on its fixture)
  while `instructions` stays equal — the wall-clock delta there was inside run-to-run noise.
- One IR construct now has one entry shape in the VM (`_start`, `command_main`, interrupts and
  thread entries), and a memory-exhaustion program hits the wall at the same point in the VM and in
  the native artefact.

## new · editions and `lgc`

Tur 1 gives the native grammar its own name (`print`, `fn main`; `rust` is a surface grammar), Tur
2026.1 adds two-level edition names and the three edition outputs, Tur 2026.2 freezes six syntax
items behind a feature ratchet, and Tur 2026.3 opens the edition with `lgc`: `lgc start;` / `lgc end;`
pause and resume collection at run time, `lgc start { … }` is a lexical window, and
`lgc start(<duration>) { … }` is a cooperative time budget.

**The default reading is now the newest edition.** A source with no `choose write grammar` is read
as `tur2026.3`; the declaration exists to pin an *older* reading (`tur` / `tur1` are the explicit way
to ask for Tur 1), not to unlock the current one. Opening a new edition would be dangerous if it
silently changed the meaning of an existing identifier, so it does not: a collision between a new
construct and an old identifier refuses to compile (E040) instead of being reinterpreted.

## fix · the 0.1.5.1 defect sweep

The recurring shape was **silence**, not crashes: a tool that reported success while writing
nothing, a renderer that blamed toolchain skew for its own fallback. Closed in this period: the
self-hosted checker no longer writes past its diagnostics buffer (`#663`) and says how many records
it dropped (`#656`); `lomenterr` no longer emits invalid UTF-8 (`#666`), control bytes from the
source (`#654`), a fabricated `E034` (`#662`), or a column where the line belongs (`#664`); a failed
write is reported as a failure instead of exit 0 (`#674`); and the launcher no longer flattens a
SIGSEGV to exit 1 (`#673`).

## known boundaries

- **Lifetimes are still a design** (Tur 2026.3): `lgc` landed, lifetimes did not.
- **The capability-domain slice covers ten of the eighteen designed kinds** (`docs/306` §12). The
  periodic domain (it needs per-slot timestamps), the generational and adaptive domains (safepoints
  and the quality ledger), the remaining context-class domains (subject, witness, flow, reachable),
  and domain trees/graphs/extension/nesting remain design.
- **`no_std` capability-chain reporting** remains `#536`; a library writing `choose` is a loader
  rule.
- **Hot update admits fix-only projections.** A contract change is refused by design, not by
  omission.
